attributes.residual: THE FRAME DELTA IS SOLVED AND THE SLOT POSITIONS ARE NOT SOURCE-REACHABLE, AND THOSE ARE TWO SEPARATE RESULTS. (1) SOLVED: the padding local must be `u8 unused[32]`, not `[24]`. That single change makes the frame size EXACTLY the target's 176 (from 168) and cuts exclusive slots from 4T/4O to 1T/1O, collapsing four rows -- target-only slots 104/176/180 and ours-only 64/168/172 all resolve, and the -176/-168 stwu displacement row closes. This is a structural convergence and it is banked here as a fact, not as a keep. (2) NOT RETAINED, AND WHY: with the frame exact, `real` rose 1195 -> 1217 and fresh objdiff fuzzy FELL 96.2610 -> 96.2573. Two of the three arbiters say revert and the project's monotonic rule decides it, so the tree is at HEAD. The keep is available to any lane that can also close the last slot row in the same commit. (3) THE RECLASSIFICATION, which is the durable finding. Three probes varying pad size, pad position and scalar declaration order produced THREE IDENTICAL slot maps -- byte-identical rows, identical real 1217 -- so beyond its total size the local declaration block does not determine these offsets at all. The nine local slots are register-allocator SPILL TEMPS, not homes of declared locals, which is why claim.law.stack-slots-descend-in-declaration-order does not transfer here and why the work order's 'pool-layout debt' framing does not fit: there is no pool row and no constant row in this residual. Two identical A/Bs kill an axis; three kill it with room to spare. (4) THE REMAINING SLOT ROW, stated exactly so the next lane need not re-derive it: with pad 32 the target's local run occupies {68,72,76,80,84,88,92,96,104} with use-counts {2,2,2,2,2,2,4,4,2} and ours occupies {72,76,80,84,88,92,96,100,104} with {4,2,2,2,2,2,2,4,2}. Nine slots each side; ours is the same run shifted up one 4-byte step, and the two 4-use temps sit at the run's two ENDS in our stream where the target has them ADJACENT at 92/96. (5) SEPARATELY, the structural half is untouched and is the bigger prize: the multiset differs by +5 add +2 addi +1 lwzx target-only against -3 li -2 lwz -1 mr ours-only, and the --ops clusters show ONE repeated idiom at roughly +0x41c, +0x724, +0x800 and +0x68c where the target emits a late `add` and we emit an earlier `addi`+`add` pair. That is an induction/addressing form, it recurs at least four times, and it is worth more than the slot row.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Read one site aligned before editing anything: `fnasm game/ui/select do_player_select 0x71c:0x74c --diff`. If the target's `add` there consumes a value that our `addi` also has to compute -- i.e. the extra word is a genuine second address, not a re-association of the same one -- then the two streams are computing different quantities and the induction framing is wrong at that site; check all four sites before generalising, because the --ops clusters at +0x41c and +0x68c are not obviously the same shape as the two at +0x724/+0x800.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- this pass measured the frame and slot halves only, and the addressing idiom is read from the fndiff --ops cluster list, NOT from the aligned view. The register-level content of all four sites is unmeasured, which is exactly what the refuting observation above buys for one command.
hypothesis.statement: The repeated addressing idiom, not the slot map, is do_player_select's next win, and it is source-reachable. At +0x724 and +0x800 the target issues a single `add` where we issue `addi`+`add`, the same shape recorded elsewhere in this project as the `base + i*stride` induction form beating a named-offset accumulator. do_player_select computes several per-player offsets (padoff, xoff, poff, boff, moff) and then indexes off them; rewriting those sites to index directly as `base + i * stride` rather than accumulating a named offset local should remove our extra `addi` at each of the four sites and move the count from O1882 toward T1885.
